A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison: Appendices A–D are retained, and v2 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D and 4D simulations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–2, plus an Oklahoma earthquake analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original 10D comparisons, no-change monitoring, and rank/partition sensitivity experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes threshold calibration from permuting individual training windows to permuting consecutive blocks, with revised group-size normalization. The matrix representation and restricted SVD remain unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 3 also omit v1's explicit outer-loop exit after an alarm, changing the written stopping procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a dependent 10D PPP setting with sinusoidal intensity changes and a sustained no-change counterpart. This substantially extends experimental coverage beyond the retained 3D/4D simulations and earthquake application. The advertised non-low-rank property requires qualification, as discussed under improvement.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds an evaluated NN-CUSUM comparator adapted from Gong et al. (2022), alongside Matrix, MMD, and KIE in Table 3 and the no-change comparison. Gong et al. was already cited in v1 but was not an evaluated baseline. The original experiments retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported calibration protocol changes to block permutations. Appendix E adds a design with 1200 training observations, change time 1400, and 1800 total observations; cumulative no-change monitoring; and controlled rank/partition comparisons. Figure 3 also changes the earthquake averaging windows. Retained original scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun under the revised calibration.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds sustained false-alarm monitoring and sensitivity tests comparing ranks 3, 5, and 10 with a random coordinate partition. These directly examine error control and structural tuning choices absent from v1's empirical analyses. The earthquake case study also expands from two intensity panels to six consecutive annual windows.

E5.justification: The empirical null-quantile estimator changes its resampling unit from individual windows to blocks, while retaining 500 permutations. Simulation reporting continues to use 100 replications and conditional ADD standard deviations. Additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice; neither version adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2, Figures 1–2, and earthquake alarm dates are unchanged. New Table 3 reports 10D ADD values of 24.21 for Matrix, 266.51 for MMD, 284.33 for KIE, and 240.10 for NN-CUSUM. Table 4 adds cumulative false-alarm results, including 4% for Matrix and 14% for KIE at time 2200. Figures 3–6 add temporal intensity, comparison, and sensitivity findings.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, assumptions, bounds, and proof arguments are retained. Lemma 8 explicitly names the Hilbert–Schmidt norm and operator restriction while preserving the existing compression argument and inequality. Remark 4 explains the scope of the existing rank condition without changing the theorem or supplying a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 retain the same central contributions: a single-pass low-rank detector, constant per-observation cost, false-alarm/delay guarantees, and a dependent-PPP matrix Bernstein inequality. The conclusion's explicit beta-mixing wording restates an assumption already present in v1. Additional experiments support retained contributions.

C2.justification: Remark 4 newly distinguishes the heuristic partition-selection rule from the theorem's approximate-rank requirement. Appendix E interprets its experiments as demonstrating rank/partition insensitivity and performance without exact low rank, although the latter premise conflicts with the stated intensity formulas. The earthquake discussion now emphasizes progressive spatial expansion after detection.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Python implementation repository link, details block construction and normalization, and describes NN-CUSUM's online discrimination and held-out scoring. These improve documentation, although the numerical block length, 10D autoregressive recurrence, and concrete neural-network settings are not supplied in the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 more explicitly distinguishes the proposed setting from parametric Hawkes detectors and offline point-process methods. The cited works are retained; updates to Wei and Xie, Shin et al., and Zhao et al. identify publication versions rather than new research sources. The substantive positioning change is confined to this targeted discussion.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites related work, expands the linearity and partition explanations, revises calibration prose, and adds Appendix E. The main narrative and existing appendix organization remain recognizable. Bibliographic formatting and conclusion wording change, but the retained paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 4–6, replaces Figure 3's two maps with six annual panels and a shared color scale, and reformats all three algorithms. Existing tables and figures move within the layout. Figure 2's caption is corrected from 3D to 4D; its plotted results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparisons, clearer earthquake chronology, partition qualifications, and code-access information. However, its central new non-low-rank validation is unsupported: the stated sine/cosine-of-sum intensities have rank at most three under any coordinate split, contradicting the claimed infinite-rank setting. Table 3 leaves the distinction between its two ADD rows unexplained, and Algorithms 1 and 3 lose their explicit stop-after-alarm check. These new reliability issues coexist with meaningful additions, preventing a confident net assessment of overall improvement.
